procedure.step: Register the factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae). Registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. Processing takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply for a Certificate of Origin for India through the e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents, pay the fee online, submit the application, and receive approval or a return with comments to correct.
Pay the certificate fee. For an invoice value up to AED 100000, the fee is AED 50 (fee range: AED 10 to AED 200).

The certificate shall be issued prior to, at or within five working days of the date of exportation. It is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and covers only one import. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 (Remarks).

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years, starting from the end of the year of the date of issue of the certificate.

caveats.note: Duty is estimated on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The '+' in the rule PSR-IN-R118 is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 read through LiveLaw and taxmann), not the official text.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
